## CLI

> 17 rules

### Flag Vocabulary

`cli:flag-vocabulary` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Define these flags once, with these names, on every command where they are meaningful; language and framework rules may document how to declare them, but must not rename them or add a second spelling (not `--yes`/`-y`, `--force`, `--plan`, `--no-input`, or `--non-interactive`). `-h`/`--help` prints usage to stdout and exits 0. `-V`/`--version` prints `<program> <semver>` to stdout, exits 0, and returns before reading configuration, touching the network, or entering the alternate screen. `-v`/`--verbose` adds diagnostics on stderr. `-q`/`--quiet` suppresses non-essential output but never errors. `--json` writes machine-readable output to stdout with no ANSI or locale-dependent formatting. `--no-color` disables ANSI and must also honor `NO_COLOR`. `-n`/`--no-interaction` never prompts: confirmation prompts are treated as answered and the command proceeds, even when the interactive default would be no. `--dry-run` prints the planned actions, applies nothing, and exits 0. Accept global flags before and after subcommands, show only the canonical names in help, and when `--dry-run` and `--no-interaction` are combined, `--dry-run` wins and nothing is written.

> URLs: [Command Line Interface Guidelines: Arguments and flags](https://clig.dev/#arguments-and-flags), [NO_COLOR](https://no-color.org/)

### Manage Keys

`cli:manage-keys` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

Every microservice MUST ship `manage-keys` binary (`create <name>`/`list`/`revoke <id>`) operating directly on key storage (DB or flat file) out-of-band, no HTTP, no `--url`/`--json`/auth. Entrypoint `src/keys_cli.py`, commands `src/commands/keys_cmd.py`; raw key printed once, redisplayable via `list` (plaintext). Works before/without API; on server via `docker compose exec app manage-keys ...`. For DB services, `{name}-migrate` wrapper runs `alembic upgrade head` then seeds.

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

### Streams

`cli:streams` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Treat stdout as the program's result and stderr as diagnostics: results, data, and machine output go to stdout; progress, warnings, prompts, and errors go to stderr. Detect TTYs independently and never emit color, spinners, or interactive prompts into a pipe. Support `--quiet` to suppress non-essential output and `--verbose` to add diagnostics on stderr unless documented otherwise.

> URLs: [Command Line Interface Guidelines: Output](https://clig.dev/#output)

### Command Grammar

`cli:command-grammar` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Use one consistent grammar, either `tool <verb> <noun>` or `tool <noun> <verb>`, and never mix both. Keep command names short, stable, and pronounceable; use kebab-case for multi-word flags and reserve single-letter flags for frequent options. Accept positional arguments only for the primary subject, put everything else behind named flags, and never give one flag context-dependent meanings.

> URLs: [Command Line Interface Guidelines](https://clig.dev/)

### Errors

`cli:errors` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Errors state what failed, why, and the exact next step in plain language, quoting the offending value and suggesting a valid alternative or `--help`. Print them to stderr, attach a stable error code or support id to unexpected failures, and show stack traces only behind `--debug` or `--trace`. Never blame the user or leave them without a recovery path.

### Exit Codes

`cli:exit-codes` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Exit 0 only on success and non-zero on every failure. Use 2 for usage errors, 1 for general runtime failures, 126 and 127 for not executable and not found, and 128+n for termination by signal n; document any additional codes. Never encode result data in exit codes, and return the most specific actionable code instead of always 1.

> URLs: [POSIX Utility Conventions](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap12.html)

### Version

`cli:version` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Every CLI and TUI tool must expose a non-interactive `--version` (and `-V` where the parser supports it) that prints `<program> <semver>` to stdout, exits 0, and returns before reading configuration, touching the network, or entering the alternate screen. Keep one source of truth for the version (package metadata or a build-time constant), include commit or build metadata only when it does not break parsing, and make the reported version match the release artifact and Git tag.

### Accessibility

`cli:accessibility` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Never rely on color alone to convey meaning; pair it with text, symbols, or position. Honor `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, and non-TTY output, preserve readable contrast, avoid rapid flashing, and make every interactive flow usable with the keyboard alone. Keep plain-text output useful when read by a screen reader or copied into an issue.

> URLs: [NO_COLOR](https://no-color.org/)

### Help

`cli:help` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Every command and subcommand supports `-h`/`--help` and prints usage to stdout with exit 0: one-line purpose, usage line, positional arguments, grouped options with defaults, a working example, and a link to further documentation. Running a parent command with no arguments prints its help, and the root command offers `--version`. Generate help from the same definitions the parser uses so it never drifts.

> URLs: [Command Line Interface Guidelines: Help](https://clig.dev/#help)

### Interactivity

`cli:interactivity` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Prompt only when stdin is a TTY and never block in CI, cron, or pipes; expose a flag or environment variable for every prompt so the command can run unattended. Confirm destructive or irreversible actions by default, allow `-n`/`--no-interaction` to skip the prompt and proceed, and make prompts cancelable with Ctrl-C (exit 130) without partial writes. Hide secret input and keep secrets out of process arguments and shell history.

> URLs: [Command Line Interface Guidelines: Interactivity](https://clig.dev/#interactivity)

### Output

`cli:output` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Default output is human-readable and scannable: aligned columns, records that never wrap into each other, and a final summary for batch work. Offer `--json` or `--format` with a stable, documented schema, one record per line, no decoration, and no human-only text on stdout. Honor `--no-color` and `NO_COLOR`, and degrade to ASCII when the locale or terminal cannot render Unicode.

> URLs: [NO_COLOR](https://no-color.org/)

### Configuration

`cli:configuration` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Resolve configuration in a documented order: explicit flag, environment variable, project config, user config, then built-in default. Use standard locations (XDG on Linux), support `--config`, validate values at startup with actionable errors, and never read or write another tool's config file. Prefer environment variables or files for secrets and support `--config -` or stdin where it avoids writing secrets to disk.

> URLs: [XDG Base Directory Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/latest/)

### Consistency

`cli:consistency` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Reuse one vocabulary and one behavior for common concerns across all commands. The canonical flag names and semantics live in `cli:flag-vocabulary`; never introduce a second spelling for the same concern. Keep destructive operations symmetric and predictable, accept global flags before and after subcommands, and reserve abbreviations for unambiguous prefixes. Match the platform's flag syntax conventions without inventing a private dialect.

### Feedback

`cli:feedback` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Acknowledge long operations on stderr within 100 ms and report a definite success or failure. Show progress for work over 1 s when stderr is a TTY, print a deterministic final summary, and make repeated runs idempotent. Never claim success before writes are durable and never leave a half-finished state without saying so.

### Composability

`cli:composability` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Follow the Unix philosophy: one command does one job well, reads stdin and writes stdout so it can be piped, and uses `-` for stdin where a file is expected. Support null-delimited output (`-0` or `--print0`) for filenames, avoid pagers when stdout is not a TTY, and keep machine-readable output free of locale-dependent formatting.

### Performance

`cli:performance` · scope **tech** · from *CLI Conventions*

Keep startup fast, stream results as they become available instead of buffering the whole run, and avoid network or disk work the command does not need. Bound external calls with timeouts and retries with backoff, make long operations cancelable, and never hide a slow step behind a silent pause.

### Client

`cli:client` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

Typer app with `CLI_CONTEXT_SETTINGS` (`-h`/`--help`) and `no_args_is_help=True`; shared `@app.callback()` holding client + `--json` flag in `ctx.obj`; subcommands call `get_client(ctx)`/`emit(ctx, ...)` from `commands/common.py`. Secrets env-only (passwords never flag); API keys may use flag+env (e.g. `--api-key`/`PACKAGE_SERVICE_API_KEY`); refuse insecure defaults for remote. Connection resolve: `--url` > env > localhost. Output Rich tables for humans, `--json` for machine; raw keys printed once with warning; `list` may redisplay plaintext (treat as secret). TLS verify on by default; `--insecure` opt-out.

## Ansible

> 10 rules

### Vault

`ansible:vault` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

Encrypt every credential with `ansible-vault` and commit only a `vault.example.yml` with placeholders. Keep `vault.yml` and the vault password out of git, pass `--ask-vault-pass` or a password file outside the repository, and never print secret values in debug output.

### Deploy

`ansible:deploy` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

Deploy from a pinned `repo_version` (tag or commit), render configuration from templates and vars, and bring the stack up with `community.docker.docker_compose_v2` using `pull: always`, `recreate: auto`, and `state: present`. Do not run ad-hoc `docker` commands on the host or leave a partial deployment.

### Idempotency

`ansible:idempotency` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

Write idempotent tasks with declarative modules (`ansible.builtin.*`, `community.docker.*`, `community.general.*`). Avoid `shell` and `command` when a module exists; when one is necessary, add `creates`, `removes`, `changed_when`, and `failed_when`. Re-running the playbook must converge without duplicating state.

### Permissions

`ansible:permissions` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

Create directories and files with explicit `owner`, `group`, and `mode`; use `0600` or `0640` for secrets and the minimum mode for configuration. Give runtime data directories the container uid/gid, and never use `0777` or recursive world-writable permissions.

### Preflight

`ansible:preflight` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

Before changing anything, verify prerequisites: Docker and Compose, required collections, external networks and volumes, DNS, disk space, and the vault. Fail with an actionable message before the first destructive task.

### Health Checks

`ansible:health-checks` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

After deployment, wait for local and public readiness endpoints with bounded `retries` and `delay`; fail on timeout and surface container logs. Print a deployment summary that includes versions and URLs but never secrets.

### Playbook Structure

`ansible:playbook-structure` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

Use one named playbook per stack under `deploy/`, run it with `become: true`, load secrets from `vars_files`, and keep tasks small and named. Support `--check` and `--diff` where modules allow, and never hide failures behind `ignore_errors` without a documented reason.

### Rollback

`ansible:rollback` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

Document and support rollback by redeploying the previous `repo_version` or image tag with the same playbook. Back up or verify state compatibility before downgrading, and record the deployed version in the summary.

### Deploy Wrapper

`ansible:deploy-wrapper` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

Provide a `deploy/deploy.sh` wrapper with `set -euo pipefail`, repository-root resolution, a missing-vault check, and `ansible-playbook -i ... --ask-vault-pass "$@"`. Keep secrets out of command-line arguments and shell history.

### Inventory

`ansible:inventory` · scope **tech** · from *Ansible Conventions*

Keep a small inventory under `deploy/hosts.ini` with one group per stack and explicit `ansible_host`, `ansible_user`, and `ansible_python_interpreter`. Never put passwords or keys in the inventory, and document how to add or move hosts.

## Auth

> 3 rules

### API Keys

`auth:api-keys` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

Every microservice MUST ship revocable API keys, storage-backed (DB table or flat file). Static env-var credential (e.g. `ADMIN_API_KEY`) never acceptable; keys must be creatable, listable, revocable without redeploy. Store raw key in plaintext, display `prefix`; raw key returned exactly once at creation, redisplayable via `manage-keys list`. Key format `sk-<svc>-` + 32 hex chars (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Soft revoke (`revoked_at`, NULL active), idempotent. `last_used_at` touched on successful auth. Use `secrets.compare_digest`. Server refuses default credential (`change-me-in-production`/`changeme`); clients refuse it for remote hosts.

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

### Key Storage

`auth:key-storage` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

Storage variants: (1) DB-backed: `api_key` table with `id`, `name` (non-empty, <=64), `raw_key` (unique plaintext), `prefix`, `created_at`, `revoked_at`, `last_used_at` via Alembic revision. (2) Flat-file (no DB): `data/api_keys.json` with same records, written atomically (temp+rename) mode `0600`, locked against concurrent access, excluded from rsync like `*.db*`. Both behind small repository/service layer.

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

### Key Management

`auth:key-management` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

Key management patterns: (1) Multi-consumer via API: distinct keys per consumer; `HTTPBasic(auto_error=False)` accepts Basic or `X-API-Key`; separate Basic-only `verify_admin_credentials` guards key management (API keys cannot manage); revoke 204 idempotent, 404 never-existing. (2) Single-admin via storage: host-local Typer `manage-keys` operates on `DATABASE_URL`/flat file, no HTTP, runs locally or `docker compose exec app manage-keys ...`; bootstrap: create key -> put into client env -> start API. Client env-var naming independent of server config.

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

## Bash

> 11 rules

### Deploy Confirmation

`bash:deploy-confirmation` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Every deployment script MUST print a summary of the planned actions before changing anything and ask for explicit confirmation before proceeding. The summary lists the target environment and hosts, the version/tag or commit being deployed, the services and configuration that will change, and every destructive step (migrations, deletions, restarts); it never prints secret values. Abort with a non-zero exit code unless the answer is an explicit yes. Support `-n`/`--no-interaction` to skip the prompt and proceed and `--dry-run` to print the same summary without applying it; require `--no-interaction` when stdin is not a TTY.

### Security

`bash:security` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Avoid using `eval`; be cautious with user-supplied input; use `readonly` for critical variables; implement proper input validation. Minimize external commands, use built-ins, check command availability, avoid bashisms if cross-shell needed, test with `shellcheck`. Include self-test mode and input validation.

### Shebang Strict

`bash:shebang-strict` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Always use the shebang `#!/usr/bin/env bash` for maximum portability. Enable strict error handling and safety modes at the beginning of the script: `set -euo pipefail`. Add comments explaining each option: `# -e: Exit immediately if a command exits with non-zero status`, `# -u: Treat unset variables as an error`, `# -o pipefail: Return exit status of last command in pipeline that failed`.

> Sources: Bash Conventions

### Error Handling

`bash:error-handling` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Define and document meaningful exit codes (0 success, 1 general, 2 misuse, 126 cannot execute, 127 not found, 128 invalid arg, 130 terminated). Consider using traps for cleanup: `trap cleanup EXIT ERR` with a cleanup function.

### Variables

`bash:variables` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Use `UPPERCASE_WITH_UNDERSCORES` for constants and global variables; `snake_case` for local variables; prefix internal/private variables with underscore `_internal_var`. Always quote variables to prevent word splitting and globbing. Use `readonly` for constants, `local` for function-scoped variables.

### Control Flow

`bash:control-flow` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Use Bash's double-bracket conditional test syntax (a pair of square brackets), prefer `==` for string comparisons, `-eq`, `-ne` etc. for integers. Use `for` loops with safe practices and quote variables in loops.

### Functions

`bash:functions` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Document each function with a comment block (purpose, behavior, arguments, returns, example). Keep functions small, focused, single responsibility, prefer pure functions. Use `return` for status codes (0 success, non-zero error) and command substitution `$()` for returning output.

### CLI Help

`bash:cli-help` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Each script should have at least `-h|--help` CLI flags and a `usage` function to document usage.

### Defaults

`bash:defaults` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Use parameter expansion for providing default values, e.g. `log_level="${LOG_LEVEL:-info}"` and `config_path="${1:-/default/path}"`.

### Header Comments

`bash:header-comments` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Include comprehensive doc header at top of each script (after shebang) with script name, creation/mod dates, detailed description, optional author and version. Write clear concise comments explaining complex logic and **why** not just **what**. Use `#` for inline comments and `# ---- ` for section comments. Use `# TODO:` for planned improvements.

### Io

`bash:io` · scope **tech** · from *Bash Conventions*

Use `echo` for standard output, `printf` for formatted output, redirect errors to `stderr` (e.g., `echo "Error: Invalid input" >&2`).

## Python Script

> 8 rules

### Metadata Format

`python-script:metadata-format` · scope **tech** · from *Python Script Conventions (PEP 723)*

Dependencies are declared in a `# /// script` TOML block at the top of the file. The `dependencies` field must be present (even if empty). `requires-python` is optional but recommended. Use a TOML array-of-tables header (a double square bracket around the table path, e.g. `tool.uv.index`) for alternative package indexes. Use `# [tool.uv]` with `exclude-newer` for reproducibility.

### Shebang

`python-script:shebang` · scope **tech** · from *Python Script Conventions (PEP 723)*

Make scripts directly executable with a `uv run --script` shebang: `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script` as the first line, before the `# /// script` block. Then `chmod +x <script>.py` to run via `./<script>.py`.

### Best Practices

`python-script:best-practices` · scope **tech** · from *Python Script Conventions (PEP 723)*

Best practices: Single file only (for multi-module use generic-python). Keep dependencies minimal, prefer stdlib. Type hints still recommended for functions. Always include a `main()` function guarded by `if __name__ == "__main__"`. Add shebang as first line for executables. Commit `<script>.py.lock` to version control. No pyproject.toml — all metadata in script. For testable logic, extract into functions tested via `pytest` run with `uv run --with pytest --script <test>.py` or inline simple assertions.

### Locking

`python-script:locking` · scope **tech** · from *Python Script Conventions (PEP 723)*

Locking: Run `uv lock --script <script>.py` to create `<script>.py.lock`. Once locked, `uv run --script`, `uv add --script`, `uv export --script`, and `uv tree --script` reuse the lockfile. For reproducibility, add `exclude-newer` to `[tool.uv]` to pin a cutoff date.

### Running

`python-script:running` · scope **tech** · from *Python Script Conventions (PEP 723)*

Run with `uv run <script>.py` — uv auto-creates an ephemeral environment. Unlike projects, `uv run` with inline metadata ignores any surrounding project's dependencies; `--no-project` is not needed. Use `uv run --python 3.10 <script>.py` to override Python version. Use `uv run --with <pkg> <script>.py` for ad-hoc dependencies (avoid; prefer inline metadata). Pass arguments normally: `uv run <script>.py --arg1 value1`.

### Use Pep723

`python-script:use-pep723` · scope **tech** · from *Python Script Conventions (PEP 723)*

Use PEP 723 inline script metadata for standalone single-file Python scripts. This format embeds dependencies and metadata directly in the script using a TOML block, managed entirely by `uv`.

> Sources: Python Script Conventions (PEP 723)

### Project Manifest

`python-script:project-manifest` · scope **tech** · from *Python Script Conventions (PEP 723)*

The project manifest (`projects/python-script.yaml`) provides variables: `{{ scriptName }}` (default `script.py`), `{{ pythonVersion }}` (default `3.13`), and `{{ partials.python_script_rules }}` (these conventions). These variables are available in snippets rendered with `--project python-script`.

### Uv Commands

`python-script:uv-commands` · scope **tech** · from *Python Script Conventions (PEP 723)*

Key uv commands for script management: `uv init --script <file>.py --python 3.12` to initialize; `uv add --script <file>.py '<package>'` to add dependency; `uv add --script <file>.py '<package>=<version>'` for version constraint; `uv run <file>.py` to run; `uv lock --script <file>.py` to lock; `uv export --script <file>.py` to export lockfile; `uv tree --script <file>.py` for dependency tree; `chmod +x <file>.py` to make executable.

## Python

> 12 rules

### Prompts

`python:prompts` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

All yes/no prompts MUST go through a single shared `confirm()` helper (located in utils.py) rather than calling InquirerPy directly. The helper uses `inquirer.select` with Yes/No choices for gum-style buttons and falls back to default when stdin is not a TTY. Destructive/mutating commands must call `confirm()` and offer `-n`/`--no-interaction` to skip the prompt and proceed. Import `confirm` from shared module; use `inquirer.select`/`fuzzy` directly only for multi-option menus.

### Basics

`python:basics` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

Use Python version 3.12+. Type hints are mandatory for functions and class methods. Follow PEP8 (https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/) and PEP257 (https://peps.python.org/pep-0257/) style guidelines. Use docstrings for modules, classes, and functions.

> Sources: Python Conventions

### Testing

`python:testing` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

Unit tests required for all new functionality. Use `pytest` framework. Aim for at least 80% test coverage. Use `black` for formatting, `ruff` or `flake8` for linting, and `mypy` for type checking (run with `uv run`).

### Dependencies

`python:dependencies` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

All dependencies defined in `pyproject.toml` (not requirements.txt). Use `uv add <package>` for app deps, `uv add --dev <package>` for dev deps. Keep minimal. Use specified libraries where appropriate: Typer, Rich, Textual, Trogon, InquirerPy (do NOT use questionary), PyYAML, FastAPI (if needed), NiceGUI/Streamlit, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, LiteLLM/PydanticAI V2.

### Integration

`python:integration` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

API Interactions: isolate API client code into dedicated modules, use environment variables for keys (`.env` with python-dotenv), implement error handling and rate limiting awareness, cache results. Configuration: use YAML files, support global (`~/.config/your_app/config.yml`) and local (`./config.yml`), implement fallbacks for missing values.

### CLI

`python:cli` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

Use Typer for all CLI functionality. Place subcommands in `commands/` directory with filenames ending `_cmd.py`. Implement comprehensive `--help`. Add `-h` as short option for `--help` via `context_settings` (defined centrally e.g. config.py) and set `no_args_is_help=True` in Typer constructor. Provide meaningful error messages and support config via CLI args and config files. Follow pattern in `cli.py`.

### Project Structure

`python:project-structure` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

Organize code in modular structure with clear separation of concerns. Use package layout with `__init__.py`. Recommended tree: project_name/ with .venv/, __init__.py, cli.py, core/, utils/, commands/ (subcommands as *_cmd.py), config.py. Avoid placing all code in a single file and avoid writing code into `__init__.py`.

### Uv

`python:uv` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

Use `uv` as the all-in-one tool for virtual environment and dependency management (replaces pip, venv, requirements.txt). For setup run `uv venv`, activate with `source .venv/bin/activate`, then `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`. Do not run `uv init`. Daily workflow: use `uv run pytest`/`uv run black .`, `uv add <pkg>` for deps, `uv add --dev <pkg>` for dev deps, `uv remove <pkg>`, `uv pip sync pyproject.toml --all-extras` to sync, `uv lock` for lockfile.

### Imports

`python:imports` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

Group imports in the following order with a blank line between groups: 1. Standard library imports, 2. Third-party imports, 3. Local application imports.

### Naming

`python:naming` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

Naming conventions: use `snake_case` for functions, variables, and modules; `PascalCase` for classes; `UPPERCASE` for constants.

### UI

`python:ui` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

UI development conventions: NiceGUI - use `ui.run()` only in main.py under `if __name__ in {"__main__", "__mp_main__"}:`, prefer `@ui.page('/')` decorators, Tailwind via `.classes()`, `app.storage` for persistent state, `bind_value`/`bind_text` for reactivity, `async def` handlers, `@ui.refreshable` for dynamic sections. Streamlit - top-to-bottom rerun model, ALWAYS use `st.session_state` with init pattern, `@st.cache_data`/`@st.cache_resource`, `on_change`/`on_click` callbacks, `st.sidebar`/`st.columns`/`st.tabs`. Textual - subclass `App`, use `compose()` to yield widgets, TCSS for styling, message handlers/`@on`, `async def`, integrate Typer with Trogon for auto TUI.

### String Formatting

`python:string-formatting` · scope **tech** · from *Python Conventions*

Prefer f-strings for string formatting.

## Config

> 1 rule

### Env Guard

`config:env-guard` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

Use `APP_ENV` (not `ENV`): `env: str = Field(default="dev", alias="APP_ENV")`. Swagger guard fail-closed: `debug = settings.env == "dev"` (never `!= "prod"`); disable `docs_url`, `redoc_url`, and `openapi_url` in non-dev. Wire `APP_ENV: prod` explicitly in production compose. Use `create_app()` factory for testability; module-level `app` needs subprocess test setting `APP_ENV=prod` before import.

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

## DB

> 1 rule

### Migrations

`db:migrations` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

Every service with a DB uses Alembic as the single standard migration mechanism (no hand-rolled `*.sql` runners, no SQLModel `create_all` + ad-hoc `ALTER`). SQLModel preferred for `alembic revision --autogenerate`; raw `sqlite3` supported with `op.execute` and `target_metadata=None`. Revision chain must have exactly one head. `migrations/env.py` MUST set `render_as_batch=True` for SQLite. Review/edit autogenerate output before committing. Tests run `alembic upgrade head` on fresh in-memory/temp SQLite and assert resulting schema. Expose `{name}-migrate` CLI wrapping `alembic upgrade head` (+ optional seed). Seed data applied by separate step after migration, never inside.

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

## Deploy

> 2 rules

### Ansible

`deploy:ansible` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

`deploy/` contains `deploy.sh`, `hosts.ini`, `playbook.yaml`, `compose.yaml.j2`. `deploy.sh`: `set -euo pipefail`, `usage()`, cd repo root, `uv sync --frozen`, read secrets from `.env` (refuse defaults), then `ansible-playbook -i deploy/hosts.ini deploy/playbook.yaml -e "key=$KEY"`. Playbook: create dirs (`/srv/{name}/app`, `/srv/{name}/data`, uv-cache) → rsync repo (exclude `.venv`,`.git`,`__pycache__`,`*.pyc`,`.pytest_cache`,`.ruff_cache`,`.env`,`*.db*`,`deploy`,`_ai`) → `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` in `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-bookworm-slim` with uv-cache volume → render compose → `docker compose up -d --remove-orphans` → smoke-check endpoint with `ansible.builtin.uri` retries. Persist DB/key file on host `/srv/{name}/data`; compose sets `APP_ENV: prod` only, no static admin key; keys bootstrapped via `docker compose exec app manage-keys create <name>`.

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

### Ports

`deploy:ports` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

Never use trap defaults `8000`, `5173`, `5432` (left free to fail loudly). Every service claims reserved backend port (`81xx` for `~/devel`, `82xx` for `/topdata`) from registry `~/devel/port-map/ports-private.yaml` / `ports-topdata.yaml`. When creating new service, add `projects.<name>` block there, then wire port into `uvicorn --port`, CORS origins, and compose/health-check URLs.

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

## API

> 2 rules

### Resource Naming

> 1 rule

#### Singular

`api:resource-naming:singular` · scope **tech** · from *REST API Conventions*

Name REST resources with a singular noun in lowercase, using kebab-case for multi-word names: `/customer`, `/customer/{id}`, `/order-line`. Never pluralize a resource segment; collections are expressed by the HTTP method and endpoint shape, not by a plural name.

### Homepage

`api:homepage` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

`GET /` returns tiny JSON info object: `name`, `version`, `description`, `contact`. Version via `importlib.metadata.version("{dist}")` with `PackageNotFoundError` fallback `"unknown"` — never hardcode. Do not advertise `/docs` or describe admin API/auth headers (public homepage).

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

## Stack

> 1 rule

### Base

`stack:base` · scope **tech** · from *Python Microservice Conventions*

API: FastAPI + uvicorn (server entry `{name}-api`). Config: pydantic-settings (`env_file=".env"`); real env vars take precedence. Client: typed httpx client in own module (e.g. `{name}_client.py`), tested with `respx`. CLI: Typer (`{name}-cli`), subcommands in `commands/*_cmd.py`. DB optional: SQLite only when persisting data, migrations via Alembic. Layout: `src/` package with `main.py`, `config.py`, `models.py`, `cli.py`, `commands/`, `services/`, `api/` (routes + dependencies), `db/`.

> Sources: Python Microservice Conventions

## Docs

> 15 rules

### Environment Variables

`docs:environment-variables` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Any project that reads environment variables MUST maintain `/docs/environment-variables.md`. Document every variable in one table with: name, purpose, type and default, required or optional, whether it is secret, a safe example value, and where it is read or which component uses it. Keep the file in sync with the code in the same change, make `.env.example` match it, and describe startup validation and failure behavior. Never write real secrets into the file.

### Code Docstrings

`docs:code-docstrings` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Every public or exported module, class, function, method, and type has a docstring in the language's convention (PEP 257, TSDoc/JSDoc, Go doc comments, rustdoc `///`, PHPDoc). Document the contract, not the implementation: purpose, parameters and their units or ranges, return value, raised errors, side effects, and thread-safety. Do not repeat information already carried by the type signature. Add a docstring to private code when its contract or algorithm is not obvious from the name and signature.

### Maintenance

`docs:maintenance` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Treat documentation as part of the change: update affected docs in the same commit or pull request, delete stale content instead of leaving it, and verify links and commands in CI (link checker, docs build, quick-start smoke test). Assign an owner or reviewer for docs and review them at release time.

### Minimum Set

`docs:minimum-set` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Every project maintains a small documentation set rooted at `README.md` and `/docs/`: `README.md` (entry point), `/docs/architecture.md`, `/docs/development.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`. Add `/docs/environment-variables.md` when the project reads environment variables, `/docs/operations.md` when it is deployed or operated as a service, `/docs/api.md` (or a generated spec) when it exposes an API, and ADRs under `_ai/technical_decisions/` for significant decisions. Link every document from the README and never create empty placeholder files.

### Changelog

`docs:changelog` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Keep `CHANGELOG.md` in Keep a Changelog format with an `Unreleased` section and SemVer versions. Group entries under Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, and Security; write them for users, link issues or pull requests, and never rewrite released entries. Update the changelog in the same pull request as the change.

> URLs: [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/)

### Code Comments

`docs:code-comments` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Comments explain intent, constraints, trade-offs, and why the code is written this way — never restate what the code already says. Keep a comment next to the code it describes and update or delete it in the same change. Never leave commented-out code; delete it and rely on version control. Mark known debt with `TODO` or `FIXME` plus an owner or issue reference. Use the language's comment syntax and the project's existing section markers consistently.

### Development

`docs:development` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

`/docs/development.md` (or `CONTRIBUTING.md`) gives exact, tested commands for prerequisites, first-time setup, running locally, tests, lint, typecheck, build, and release. State required tool versions and how to seed or reset local data. Keep commands copy-pasteable and update them in the same change that alters the workflow.

### Readme

`docs:readme` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

The README is the entry point and must cover, in order: what the project does and who it is for, prerequisites, installation, a copy-pasteable quick start, configuration (link to `/docs/environment-variables.md`), development and test commands (link to `/docs/development.md`), and the license. Keep it short and move detail into `/docs/` with links.

### Adr

`docs:adr` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Record significant, hard-to-reverse decisions as ADRs in the project's ADR directory (`_ai/technical_decisions/` in these repositories) with status, context, decision, consequences, and alternatives considered. Follow the repository's existing filename and numbering pattern, never delete or rewrite accepted ADRs, and supersede one with a new ADR that cross-links both.

### API

`docs:api` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Any project that exposes an API (HTTP, IPC, CLI, or library) must document its contract in `/docs/api.md` or a generated spec (OpenAPI, JSON Schema, or rustdoc). Cover authentication, request and response examples, error codes and their meaning, pagination and limits, versioning, and the deprecation policy.

### Architecture

`docs:architecture` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

`/docs/architecture.md` explains the system at a glance: context and goals, major components and their responsibilities, boundaries and data flow, key runtime dependencies, and important trade-offs. Include a text-based diagram (Mermaid preferred) that is versioned with the code, and link ADRs for decisions instead of duplicating their rationale.

### Code Examples

`docs:code-examples` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Every non-obvious public API has a short, runnable example with realistic identifiers and values and its expected output. Run examples in CI (doctest, an `examples/` directory, or a snippet test) so they cannot rot. Mark examples that cannot run as illustrative and keep them out of the test harness.

### Code Reference

`docs:code-reference` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Generate the API reference from source annotations and docstrings with the language's standard tool (Sphinx/autodoc, TypeDoc, rustdoc, godoc, phpDocumentor); never maintain a parallel hand-written reference. Version the generator configuration with the code, fail CI when the documentation build breaks, and link the generated reference from `README.md` and `/docs/`. Hand-written guides may explain the reference but must not duplicate signatures.

### Operations

`docs:operations` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Deployable services maintain `/docs/operations.md`: environments and topology, deploy and rollback procedure, configuration and secret injection, database migrations, backup and restore, health checks, monitoring and alerting, and a troubleshooting table of symptom to cause to action. Include the exact commands and expected output for each runbook step.

### Style

`docs:style` · scope **global** · from *Documentation Conventions*

Write documentation in plain language, present tense, active voice, and second person. Use descriptive headings, short paragraphs, fenced code blocks with a language tag, and relative links that work in the repository. Prefer text over screenshots for commands and configuration; date version-specific statements and state prerequisites before steps.

## Release

> 2 rules

### Git Tags

`release:git-tags` · scope **global** · from *Release & Versioning Conventions*

Publish releases as annotated Git tags named `v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>` (for example `v1.4.0`), with `-alpha.N`, `-beta.N`, or `-rc.N` for pre-releases. Tag the exact commit that produced the published artifact, sign tags where possible (`git tag -s`), and push them explicitly with `git push origin <tag>`. Never move, force-update, or delete a published tag; publish a new version instead. The tag name must match the version in the package manifest and changelog.

> URLs: [git-tag documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-tag)

### Semver

`release:semver` · scope **global** · from *Release & Versioning Conventions*

Version numbers follow Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Bump MAJOR for incompatible changes, MINOR for backward-compatible features, and PATCH for backward-compatible fixes. Pre-releases use `-alpha.N`, `-beta.N`, or `-rc.N`; build metadata uses `+...` and never affects precedence. Keep one source of truth for the version and make package manifests, app metadata, changelog entries, and release artifacts agree.

> URLs: [Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html)
